videos.title: Focus on one thing per quarter to succeed faster - click link in bio for my new app :)
videos.description:
What would happen if you committed to one thing for the next 90 days?

Most of us into personal development have goals scattered in every direction:

👉 Progress in the day job

👉 Progress in the side hustle

👉Better health

👉 More present with the family

👉 A creative hobby

👉 Growing a personal brand

The problem is we make a tiny amount of progress in each direction.

But if we pick one thing, the one most important, needle-moving thing, and make that our primary focus for 90 days, we can make absolutely enormous progress in that one area 🚀

Loads of people have talked about this: Gary Keller in The One Thing (@the1thingbook). @gregorymckeown in Essentialism. @cal.newport in Slow Productivity.

So ask yourself: if everything else stayed the same, what's the one area where a concerted effort would have the most needle-moving impact over the next 90 days?

Then carve out the time to just do that one thing.

If you want help protecting that time, my team and I have an app called Superfocus that helps you stay focused on your goals and make progress each week.

Click the link in my bio to join as a founding member :)

videos.title: Sugar Expert: Change This One Meal to Feel Better All Day | Jessie Inchauspé
videos.description:
You give your body glucose so it can make energy. Give it too much, too fast, and the same fuel starts aging you.

In this clip, Jessie Inchauspé and Jay Shetty break down what actually happens in your body when your blood sugar spikes, from your mitochondria going on strike to your cells slowly “browning” like chicken in the oven, followed by the crash that hits about 90 minutes later, disguised as a craving.

Jessie explains why breakfast is the meal that decides how your whole day feels, the study where changing nothing but the order of a meal cut the spike by 75%, and the ten years of anxiety and brain fog that led her to a glucose monitor in the first place.

Learn about the hidden sugars sitting in foods marketed as healthy, and why the restaurant bread basket might be the most profitable thing on the menu.

JAY'S DAILY WISDOM DELIVERED STRAIGHT TO YOUR INBOX
Join 900,000+ readers discovering how small daily shifts create big life change with my free newsletter. Subscribe https://news.jayshetty.me/subscribe

videos.title: The biggest barrier to AI adoption is not fear of technology. It's the absence of muscle memory.
videos.description: She used to give students a perfectly engineered prompt to get a quick win, thinking people need to feel the benefits first. Her students told her that actually made it worse. What they needed was the habit: a Slack reminder to screenshot whatever they are looking at and bring it to Claude, no pressure, no outcome required.
